html:
Station Hypo was the United States Navy's codebreaking unit at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, led by Commander Joseph Rochefort. It worked in a windowless basement and read parts of the Japanese naval code that the Americans called JN-25.

Its analysts could not read every message, but they pieced together enough to tell the Navy where Japan would attack. In spring 1942 they found that the target, called "AF", was Midway, and the Navy had its carriers waiting at the Battle of Midway. In April 1943 the unit read the travel plan of Admiral Yamamoto, which led to Operation Vengeance.

Both successes came from patient work with codes, and they changed the course of the Pacific War.
